newsitem.title: CHINA: Strong debut seen for Alpha General.
newsitem.headline: Strong debut seen for Alpha General.

text.p: Shares of appliance distributor Alpha General (Holdings) Ltd are expected to make a strong debut on Thursday with its low offering price attracting many short term investors, analysts said.

"The shares of HK$1.00 each are not pricey compared with other recent new listings which are high above this level, and that will attract smaller and short term investors," said Pamela Lam, analyst at Pacific Challenge Securities.

"A relatively warm flotation response, led by the popularity of its products in Hong Kong, has indicated strong investor interest in the stock," said Kinson Au, research manager at Asia Financial Securities.
Analysts said the grey price of the stock was about HK$1.15 each on Tuesday.
Alpha General is engaged in importing, distributing and servicing "General" brand air-conditioners, refrigerators and washing machines in Hong Kong, Macau and China.
It offered 80.9 million new shares at HK$1.00 each, with warrants attached in the proportion of one warrant for every five shares subscribed.
The offering was 41 times subscribed, the highest among new stocks listed since Hong Kong was unified with China on July 1.
In addition Fujitsu General Ltd has agreed to subscribe five percent of the enlarged issue share of Alpha General at the offer price.
"The company's earnings are seen stable and secure in the medium run because it is supplying appliances to some major housing developments in Hong Kong," Au said.
Analysts said a relatively high dividend yield of seven percent would help demand for the stock, compared with other recent new listings with yields of only three to four percent.
"However, the company reliance on a (distribution) business and on a brand name can be risky in the long run and that will discourage people to hold the stock for long," Lam said.
Alpha General had said the HK$71 million total net proceeds of the issue would be used to enhance penetration into China.
